clue.text: Single male put out about concert being unrehearsed

parts.note: single is one, written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: put out reads as the word put knocked out of shape, so its letters join the concert in a new order

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

explanation.surface: A bachelor ruins his concert preparations by going on stage without a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link: the anagram works on put and the concert together, and the result follows I and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done impromptu is improvised on the spot, with no practice beforehand.

clue.text: Inspire learner to abandon depressed profession?

indicators.note: the learner is to leave the phrase, so that letter is taken out of it

parts.note: a profession is a declaration, and declaring oneself depressed is saying I'm blue
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A trainee walks out of a gloomy career, hoping to find inspiration elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profession' looks like a job but means an avowal: the statement I'M BLUE, from which L leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue someone is to fill or permeate them with a feeling or idea, as inspiring does.

clue.text: Ceremony requiring a severe hairstyle

parts.note: pomp is stately ceremony and display
dour means stern and severe

explanation.surface: A formal ceremony demands that everyone wear a strict hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a style with the hair swept high up off the forehead.

clue.text: Official appointed to check beef

parts.note: reads like a meat inspector, but beef is slang for a complaint, and this official investigates grievances against public bodies

explanation.surface: A food inspector is sent to examine the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is a public official who investigates complaints from citizens.

clue.text: This is her top pay, unfortunately, as health worker

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so these words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A clinician complains that this is the most she will ever be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A physiotherapist treats injury and illness by exercise and massage, a health professional.

clue.text: Impassive brute raising point in a French case

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the altered brute sits inside the grammatical case

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case

indicators.note: the point, the compass letter E, is lifted up to the front of the brute's word in this down clue

parts.note: a monster is a cruel brute

explanation.surface: A thug sharpens a weapon while sitting in a French court case without a flicker of emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, east, and 'raising' lifts it to the top of the brute's word, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An undemonstrative person shows no outward emotion, which is what being impassive means.

clue.text: Discharge leader of brigade at the end of March?

parts.note: a march, as a protest, is a demo; the question mark flags that it is not the month

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brigade commander is released from service at the end of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end of' places B after DEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob, short for demobilise, means to release someone from military service.

clue.text: Bought it about noon and had a meal

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the slang word goes around noon's letter

parts.note: bought it is slang for was killed, so died

explanation.surface: Someone bought lunch around midday and ate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dined means ate dinner or another meal.

clue.text: Girl named in many a song

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, so many
an aria is a song, as in opera

explanation.surface: A girl's name crops up in many a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a song title, but 'many' is the Roman numeral M and 'a song' an ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a girl's name heard in many songs, for example in West Side Story and The Sound of Music.

clue.text: British successfully take fences, for example, to prison

parts.note: taking fences is an example of what a horse rider does, so ride
well means successfully

explanation.surface: British showjumpers clear fences well on their way to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell was a London house of correction, and the name became a general word for a jail.

clue.text: Aircraft compartment originally built in old Indian city

indicators.note: in means inserted into, so the letter goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Bombay is the old name of Mumbai

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of built

explanation.surface: A section of an aircraft was first built in the Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb bay is the part of a military plane where bombs are held for dropping.

clue.text: Old coins and notes one Asian country rejected

parts.note: D and E are both musical notes

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the country's name is read backwards

parts.note: Iran is a country in Asia
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Ancient money and banknotes are refused by an Asian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Denarii are silver pieces from ancient Rome, one denarius each.

clue.text: Animal found in Venezuelan desert

indicators.note: found in says the letters lie inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A creature is spotted in the deserts of Venezuela.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Time, perhaps, to involve press and broadcasters without delay

indicators.note: to involve means to take inside, so the rearranged letters wrap around the press
perhaps hints the word time may take another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the media are newspapers, radio and television together

explanation.surface: It may be time to get the newspapers and TV involved straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TIME to IMTE, which takes in MEDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means instant, happening at once.

clue.text: After midnight, appear indistinctly in partial darkness

indicators.note: after places the dim appearance after the middle letter

parts.note: midnight is the middle of night, its central letter
to loom is to appear dimly as a vague shape

explanation.surface: In the small hours a dark shape is dimly seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' gives the middle letter of night, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is semi-darkness, poor light.

clue.text: Great explosion involving a certain fuel tank

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the scrambled letters surround the rest
an explosion blows things apart, so the letters of great are scattered

parts.note: certain, as in a certain person, means some

explanation.surface: A huge blast involves a particular tank of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' turns GREAT into GTER, which takes in A and SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large container for storing town gas.

clue.text: Can finally made to contain passion fruit

indicators.note: to contain means holding something inside, so the can wraps round the passion

parts.note: a can is a tin
anger is a strong passion

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of made

explanation.surface: A tin is finally made to hold passion fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passion fruit' looks like one item, but 'passion' is ANGER and 'fruit' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Teams given directions to supply refreshments

parts.note: football and cricket teams are elevens, eleven players each
E is east, a compass direction
S is south, another compass direction

explanation.surface: Sports sides are told where to go to provide snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a British word for a mid-morning snack with tea or coffee.

clue.text: Produce mixture of ripe corn and wheat, ultimately?

indicators.note: a mixture mixes things together, so these letters are combined in a new order
ultimately points to the last letter of wheat

explanation.surface: A farmer blends ripe corn with wheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercrop is to grow, or produce, two crops together in one field.

clue.text: Binding English books with thin cord

parts.note: string is thin cord
NT, the New Testament, is a group of biblical books

explanation.surface: A bookbinder ties English volumes together with cord.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent means strict and binding, as with tight rules.

clue.text: Lavishly praise Abraham's nephew, backed by former wife?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, here a former wife

indicators.note: backed means turned round to face the other way, so the nephew's name is read from its end

parts.note: Lot is the nephew of Abraham in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone sings the praises of a biblical figure, supported by an ex-wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link joining the reversed nephew to the ex-wife, who comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly and enthusiastically.

clue.text: Old woman accepting mad role, perhaps, in sensational play

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so mother surrounds the rest

parts.note: ma, a mother, is an old woman in slang

indicators.note: perhaps hints these words could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: An elderly actress takes on a crazy part in a lurid drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' reads as the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'perhaps' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a play with exaggerated characters and sensational events.

clue.text: People bend over backwards to perform in this prison

definitions.text: People bend over backwards to perform in this
definitions.meaning: a Caribbean dance where people lean back to pass under a low bar

explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is both the bar-dancing contest and, informally, a place of imprisonment.

clue.text: If appeal is successful, one gets a duck

definitions.text: If appeal is successful, one gets a duck

parts.words: If appeal is successful, one gets a duck
parts.note: reads as a cricket appeal leaving a batsman out for nothing, but here a male bird whose appeal wins over a female mate

explanation.surface: In cricket, a successful appeal may send a batsman off without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of nought; here it is the female bird won by a male's charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, who wins a mate if attractive enough.

clue.text: It has no potential for connection from our home

definitions.text: It has no potential for connection
definitions.meaning: an electrical connection at zero voltage, the ground wire

explanation.definitionFit: Earth is both the zero-voltage electrical ground and the world we inhabit.

clue.text: Grasping woman's yen to accompany stringed instrument

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument
Y is the symbol for yen, Japanese money

explanation.surface: A greedy woman has a longing to play the harp.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpy is a greedy, grasping or shrewish woman, after the monsters of Greek myth.

clue.text: Having copper bowls, they produce rolls in the kitchen

definitions.text: Having copper bowls, they produce rolls in the kitchen

parts.words: Having copper bowls, they produce rolls in the kitchen
parts.note: sounds like baking bread in a kitchen, but kitchen is slang for an orchestra's percussion section, and the rolls are drum rolls

explanation.surface: Bakers use copper mixing bowls to make bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: In orchestral slang the 'kitchen' is the percussion section.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums with copper bowls, played with rolls in the percussion section.

clue.text: One whose policy is to protect someone at risk

definitions.text: One whose policy is to protect someone at risk

parts.words: One whose policy is to protect someone at risk
parts.note: sounds like a guardian's principle, but policy is an insurance document covering a customer against loss

explanation.surface: A protector's guiding principle is shielding vulnerable people.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer is a company that issues policies to cover clients against risk.

clue.text: Runs to edge of river

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to hone is to sharpen an edge

explanation.surface: Someone races to the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river of Switzerland and France.

clue.text: The old girl's religious system

parts.note: Sophy is a girl's name, the possessive adding nothing

explanation.surface: An elderly woman's belief system.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical religious philosophy seeking direct knowledge of God.
